title: Hand Wash and Dish Wash by Percentage Formula

say: Liquid Hand Wash and Dish Wash by Percentage Formula. This is module 2 of the course.
Today you'll mix a mild hand wash in the bucket, thicken it without spoiling it, and choose a dish liquid by real plate counts.

shots.label: Weighing by percentage

card.title: Hand wash starting formula
card.note: Plus EDTA 0.1%, fragrance 0.4%, citric acid as needed

say: Everything you see going onto this scale is weighed as a percentage of the batch.
That way the same sheet works for a 2 kg test or a 200 kg batch. You just multiply.
This is a starting formula for test batches. Active matter comes to 9.9%, a moderate level for hands.

card.title: Chiamaka's 10 kg batch
card.note: EDTA 10 g, preservative 80 g, fragrance 40 g

say: Chiamaka in Enugu wanted 10 kg, about 20 bottles of 500 ml. She multiplied each percentage by 10,000 g and divided by 100.
Then she added every line to check it came to exactly 10,000 g, and ticked each weight as it went in.

shots.label: Gloves and goggles
say: Gloves and goggles on before you open the SLES paste or fragrance oil. Both can irritate skin and eyes.

shots.label: Water, EDTA, then SLES paste
say: Here's the clean drum. Weigh in the water, keep back about 10% for later, and stir in the EDTA until it dissolves.
Now the SLES paste goes in, in pieces, while the paddle moves slowly. Stir gently so you don't whip in air.
When it's smooth with no lumps, add the CAPB and glycerin and stir until even.

shots.label: Fragrance premixed with CAPB
say: Watch the dropper. Premix the fragrance with a little CAPB first, so the hand wash doesn't turn cloudy.
Then add the preservative and any colour.

shots.label: pH check after 15 minutes
say: Let it rest for 15 minutes, then dip a strip. You're aiming for about 5.5 to 6.5.
If it's high, bring it down with citric acid solution, sample first, exactly as you learned in module 1.

shots.label: Four 200 g samples

card.title: Ruth's salt step test
card.note: Flow time from a syringe, 50 ml to 10 ml mark

say: Salt thickens up to a peak, then the liquid goes thin again, and you can't take salt out.
So Ruth in Jos weighed four 200 g samples and salted each one differently.
Thickness rose to 1.5% and fell at 2.0%. Her peak was around 1.5%, which fit her 15 to 25 second specification.

shots.label: Salt added as brine
shots.banner: Add salt last, after pH, in portions
say: Now watch it thicken. Ruth dissolved her 300 g of salt in 1,200 g of kept-back water to make a 20% brine.
She poured it in three portions, stirring and testing after each. The batch reached about 20 seconds without passing the peak.

shots.label: Rested overnight, then filled
say: Rest the batch covered overnight so bubbles rise. Then check it against your specification and your standard sample, and fill.
A batch that fails is held back and corrected, never sold because it's almost fine.

card.title: Zainab's plate test, 5 ml dose
card.note: Her own approximate costs: A ₦1,400/kg, B ₦1,050/kg

say: Dish liquid has a harder job. In her notebook, Zainab in Kano tested two formulas the same way: 2 g of oil on each plate, 5 litres of warm water, a 5 ml dose.
She washed until the foam disappeared and counted plates. Formula A cost more per litre but less per plate, and beat the market brand. She chose A.

shots.label: Dish wash pH about 6 to 8
say: Test the dish liquid too. Keep it around 6 to 8, gentle on hands that soak for a long time.
Never add caustic soda or soda ash for extra power. It irritates skin and can dull aluminium pots.

shots.label: Proper detergent bottles
shots.banner: Never pack dish liquid in drink bottles
say: Look at these bottles on the stall: proper detergent bottles with a label.
Never use old soft-drink or water bottles. Someone may drink from it. Print "Keep out of reach of children" and the first aid line.

shots.label: 1% dye stock solution
say: Cosmetic dyes are very strong, so make a 1% stock solution and dose that instead.
When something goes wrong, change only one thing per test sample and write it down.
Now go through the lessons below. Make your 2 kg test batch, run your own plate test, and draw your salt curve. Your numbers will tell you what works.
